title: Counterfactual config-perturbation harness for attributing latency vs. quality deltas
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: build an automated, auditable harness that performs small, counterfactual perturbations to batching and prefix/KV cache configs and attributes observed token-level and slice-level quality deltas to those config changes while correlating latency P50/P95/P99 impacts. This ticket covers the instrumentation, experiment orchestration, decision rules for safe rollouts, and a lightweight explainability layer to surface likely causal drivers for regressions.

Motivation: We frequently adjust batching shapes, microbatch TTLs, and cache eviction/prefix-merge settings to win latency/cost tradeoffs. Current LQ (latency-quality) monitoring flags anomalies but lacks a causal testbed: teams can't reliably distinguish model drift, workload shift, or config-induced regressions. A counterfactual perturbation harness will help us produce high-confidence attribution for small config changes and enable automated rollback/fallback decisions in the rollout system.

Scope:
- Orchestration layer to run paired counterfactual trials (A = baseline config, B = small delta) on matched traffic slices or synthetic replay.
- Lightweight perturbation types: microbatch-size +/- 10-30%, TTL +/- 1-3s, prefix-cache-policy toggles (merge-on-read vs merge-on-write), token-packing thresholds.
- Metrics capture: token-level logprob deltas, semantic-similarity (BERTScore), acceptability/validations (binary), hallucination proxy (NER/QA-based divergence), P50/P95/P99 latency, p95 GPU util, token throughput.
- Slice-driven evaluation: run experiments per customer-visible slice (route, prompt-template, region, tenant tier) to detect localized regressions.
- Statistical tests and confidence: paired bootstrap and A/B significance tests with minimum effect-size thresholds.
- Decision rules: confidence + minimum quality delta (e.g., >0.5 BERTScore drop or >3% acceptability loss) + latency improvement threshold triggers an approval/rollback suggestion.
- Integrations: Redwood Console dashboards, rollout canary hooks, alerting, and PRD/Confluence artifact links.

Non-goals: full ML explainability research into model internals; large-scale full-model retraining. This is focused on config-level attribution for serving changes.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run paired counterfactuals across at least 5 production slices with reproducible results
Results stored to the experiment DB with slice + config metadata and metric time series
Automated statistical test module returns significance and effect-size with configurable thresholds
Console integration: per-experiment dashboard tile and a linkable summary for rollout checks
Rollback recommendation produced when configured rules are met and validated on two historical regressions
tasks: Design experiment schema and storage (experiment id, config-delta spec, slice-id, seed)
Implement paired-run orchestration with live traffic mirroring and synthetic replay fallbacks
Instrument token-level quality hooks (logprobs, acceptability validators) in runtime tracing
Add statistical analysis module (paired bootstrap + t-test fallback) and effect-size computation
Wire results to Console/dashboard and create a reviewable summary view
Create runbook for triage and automated rollback suggestion logic
Run 3 pilot experiments (internal workloads + 2 customer-like slices) and capture learnings
comments: 2025-01-16 - Maya Chen: Kicked off design doc; initial requirements and non-goals posted to Confluence. Suggested starting with microbatch-size and TTL perturbations because they are lowest-risk and highest-signal.

2025-01-20 - Arjun Patel: Implemented the experiment schema and stubbed the orchestration service. Ran quick local paired-run with synthetic replay; observed noisy BERTScore signal for short prompts — need larger sample size per slice.
2025-01-22 - QA: Suggest adding an acceptability validator using our current QA harness to reduce false positives from semantic-similarity metrics.

2025-01-24 - Data Science (Nora Li): Proposed paired-bootstrap as primary test and Cohen's d for effect-size. Recommended minimum N=200 responses per slice for stable BERTScore estimates on short prompts.
2025-01-26 - Arjun Patel: Added token-level logprob capture and a fast NER-based hallucination proxy, and pushed integration PR: runtime#6142. Running pilot A/B on internal demo routes now.

2025-01-29 - Maya Chen: Pilot 1 results: microbatch -15% reduced P95 latency but a 1.2 point drop in average BERTScore on a short-chat slice (p<0.01, d=0.28). Flagged for follow-up: examine if KV cache prefix-merge policy can recover quality without latency loss. Preparing canary policy change playbook.
decision_records: Use paired counterfactuals over time-shifted baselines to reduce workload drift confounding
Start with small-magnitude perturbations (<=30% change) to discover safe operating directions
Require two independent slice confirmations before automated rollback is suggested (to avoid noisy single-slice flips)
notes: This harness is intended to be the canonical way we validate small serving config tweaks before wide rollouts. The outputs will also feed into Optimize for recommending safe config deltas per workload.
